title: Serialize generated content instead of interpolating JSON
environment: Observed Dify raw-text HTTP to Apps Script flow. This is a serialization correction, not proof that every stored field is semantically correct.
goal: Send canonical fields and generated text through an HTTP JSON request.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Quoted raw-text JSON templates were assumed safe for arbitrary generated text.
what_worked: Historical correction: Build one complete payload object and serialize it once; give the HTTP node only the finished JSON string. Verification reported by the source: The diagnostic request then returned creation success/HTTP 200, stored nonempty generated fields and reported parse success. Existing records were not changed during that diagnostic.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: The receiver rejected a POST with parse_invalid_json even though content type and body type looked correct.
why: Confirmed in the recorded diagnosis: quotes and newlines from generated content broke the interpolated JSON.
improved_method: Serialize structured values at the final boundary rather than concatenating JSON. Include quotes, line breaks, Unicode, arrays and objects in sender-to-receiver tests.
when_to_use: Observed Dify raw-text HTTP to Apps Script flow. This is a serialization correction, not proof that every stored field is semantically correct.
when_not_to_use: This is a serialization correction, not proof that every stored field is semantically correct.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
